land.text: Syria, ruled by the Ba'ath Party since the coup of 8 March 1963

predecessors.note: The same state: only Cliopatria's row changes at 1966/1967; the neo-Ba'athist coup was on 23 February 1966.

land.text: Syria less the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights

successors.note: The same state again: the Cliopatria row 'Syria' begins in 1973 (Wikidata Q41137, which it shares with Assyria and which is wrong for this state; Q858 is Syria).

capitals.name: Damascus
capitals.note: The Syria page: 'Capital: Damascus, which is also the largest city'.

keyframe_review.note: 1967-1968, 185,909 km2 against the Syria infobox's 185,180 km2 (ratio 1.00; no year on the page): Syria without most of the Golan Heights. It lacks 8 of the 10 cells of the gazetteer's Golan region that the Republic of Syria shape has, in line with 'two-thirds of the Golan Heights' taken 'in under 48 hours' (Syria page) and 'captured the Golan Heights on 9-10 June' (Golan page); the Syrian-held remainder is small enough to leave. Reviewer me-10-k (2026-10-25): verdict ok changed to adjust. Occupied land is hatched in the occupier's colour over the owner's (master plan rule 4; state-of-kuwait 1990 in this batch and lebanon 1983-2005 do the same), and Cliopatria's shape drops the Golan cells, which would leave the occupation hatch over no owner (and in January-June 1967 cut the Golan before the war). The correction is the 1963-1966 shape.

correction.text: Syria in its pre-war line with the Golan Heights: the Golan, occupied by Israel from June 1967, stays Syria's land under the hatch of the ledger's occupation event

keyframe_review.note: 1969-1972, the same cells and area as the 1967 shape. Nothing on the pages moves Syria's border between the Six-Day War and the 1973 war ('On 6 October 1973, Syria and Egypt initiated the Yom Kippur War'); the Corrective Movement of November 1970 changes the regime, not the land. Reviewer me-10-k (2026-10-25): verdict ok changed to adjust. Occupied land is hatched in the occupier's colour over the owner's (master plan rule 4; state-of-kuwait 1990 in this batch and lebanon 1983-2005 do the same), and Cliopatria's shape drops the Golan cells, which would leave the occupation hatch over no owner (and in January-June 1967 cut the Golan before the war). The correction is the 1963-1966 shape.

correction.text: Syria in its pre-war line with the Golan Heights: the Golan, occupied by Israel from June 1967, stays Syria's land under the hatch of the ledger's occupation event

ledger.note: 1967: Syria, ruled by the neo-Ba'athists, is drawn as the Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party row. The page says the party 'ruled Syria from the 1963 coup d'état' and that the 1966 coup was 'carried out by the radical left-wing faction of Salah Jadid and Hafez al-Assad'; the year 1967 is Cliopatria's row boundary and the page does not date it, so this is a bridging judgment, not a founding.

region.text: the Golan Heights, of which Israel took 'two-thirds ... in under 48 hours' (Syria page); the Golan page puts the part Israel holds today at 1,070 km2 plus 100 km2 of the Hermon slopes

ledger.note: 9-10 June 1967: Israel takes the Golan Heights. 'the Israel Defense Forces captured the Golan Heights on 9-10 June'; the Syria page adds that Israel captured 'two-thirds of the Golan Heights in under 48 hours'. The Golan Heights Law of 14 December 1981 later 'effectively annexed' it, declared 'null and void' by Security Council Resolution 497, so the occupation outlasts this dossier and its occupation_end belongs to the 'syria' dossier.

November 1970: Hafez al-Assad takes power. 'the Corrective Revolution of November 1970, when al-Assad ousted and imprisoned Atassi and Jadid'; the Syria page calls it 'a bloodless military coup that installed Hafez al-Assad as the strongman of the government'. Same state, same land, new ruler.
1972: Cliopatria's Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party row ends and its 'Syria' row begins in 1973 over the same cells. Not the end of a state: a row boundary that no page dates, bridged by the researcher.

wars.name: Six-Day War (Syrian front)
wars.outcome: Israel took the Golan Heights from Syria on 9-10 June 1967; the cease-fire line became the 'Purple Line'. The same war took Sinai and Gaza from Egypt and the West Bank from Jordan (see united-arab-republic).
wars.note: The Six-Day War page was opened for the UAR dossier; it says Syria 'largely stayed out of the conflict for the first four days' and accepted a cease-fire on 9 June.

certainty.note: Frontiers follow the French-mandate and armistice lines; the Golan edge is a cease-fire line (the 'Purple Line'), which the Golan page names without a date, and is only as sharp as the line held.

notes: Written by me-10-k on 2026-10-25 from four pages. This Cliopatria row (Wikidata Q16243030, the party's Syria Region article) is the Syrian state in 1967-1972, drawn under the name of the ruling party; its 185,909 km2 shape is Syria without the Golan. It is the same state as republic-of-syria (1961-1966, Q858), second-syrian-republic and syria (1973-2024); I kept it as its own dossier because the brief owns it and it has its own Wikidata id, and the colour registry already gives it the republic-of-syria hue. The founding year 1967 is the row's, not an event: the regime change was 23 February 1966 (recorded in republic-of-syria). Both ends of the row are boundaries of Cliopatria, hence the two confidence-1 events. The Golan occupation continues past 1972 (Yom Kippur War 1973, the 1974 disengagement that restored Quneitra and a third of the Golan, the 1981 law): the occupation_end belongs to 'syria', so the validator warns of an unpaired occupation_start. The Federation of Arab Republics (Egypt, Syria, Libya; referendums 1 September 1971, effective 1 January 1972, ended 19 November 1977) is an association with no territory and needs only an umbrella dossier. Not opened (page budget): the Syrian intervention in Jordan in September 1970 ('Black September'), which held no ground.
